317734.title: Minimality conjecture for the generating sets of $J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}$
317734.literal: Let $v_{r,s,t,n}$ be the bigrassmannian permutation used in type $A$, and let $J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}$ be its ideal. The two generating sets for this ideal given in Theorem~ are the generating sets under consideration. **Minimality conjecture.** Both generating sets are minimal. This has been verified computationally for all bigrassmannian permutations with $r\leq 4$ and $n-r\leq 5$; the conjecture would imply exponential lower bounds on the number of generators needed for certain ideals.
317734.gap: Need an irredundancy certificate in the actual J_v for BOTH stated generating sets at arbitrary r,s,t,n. Literal omits theorem label; source definition binding unpaid.

316252.title: Normality and Cohen–Macaulayness conjecture for Gaussian Bayesian network ideals
316252.literal:
Let $G$ be a graph for a Gaussian Bayesian network, let $I_G$ be its vanishing ideal, and let $4\mathbb{C}[\Sigma]4$ be the polynomial ring in the covariance coordinates.

**Normality and Cohen–Macaulayness conjecture.** The quotient ring

$$
\mathbb{C}[\Sigma]/I_G
$$

is normal and Cohen–Macaulay for all $G$.

The conjecture was verified computationally for all graphs on at most five vertices and for six-vertex graphs with fewer than eight edges. It is proved in the paper when the underlying graph is a tree, while the general assertion remains open.
316252.gap: Need normality and Cohen-Macaulayness for arbitrary directed Gaussian Bayesian graphs, not just source-known trees. No integral closure or depth argument established. Shared-source history 316253 is a distinct Gorenstein tree problem; its park does not settle this.

365345.title: Hall–Littlewood positivity for q-divided symmetrized Schubert polynomials
365345.literal:
Let $cmathfrak{S}_{w}cin coperatorname{Pol}_n$ be a Schubert polynomial, and let $clangle cmathfrak{S}_{w}crangle_n^q$ denote its $q$-divided symmetrization. For a partition $clambda=(clambda_1cgeq cdots cgeq clambda_n)$, let $P_{clambda}(x_1,cdots,x_n;q^{-1})$ be the Hall–Littlewood $P$-polynomial with parameter $q^{-1}$. **Hall–Littlewood expansion conjecture.** For every Schubert polynomial $cmathfrak{S}_{w}cin coperatorname{Pol}_n$, there are Laurent polynomials $b_{clambda,w}(q)$ with nonnegative integer coefficients such that

$$
clangle cmathfrak{S}_{w}crangle_n^q=csum_{clambda=(clambda_1cgeq cdots cgeq clambda_n)}b_{clambda,w}(q)P_{clambda}(x_1,cdots,x_n;q^{-1}).
$$

This generalizes the earlier Hall–Littlewood positivity prediction and was verified in the source for all permutations up to $S_8$; the general case remains open.
365345.gap: Need Hall-Littlewood coefficient nonnegativity for EVERY q-divided symmetrized Schubert polynomial. A finite positive example does not establish the all-permutation claim; actual operator normalization unread.

352588.title: Genus-independent topological-recursion formula for bipartite quadrangulations
352588.literal:
Let $E=e\,\mathrm{id}_N$ be the external matrix of the quartic Kontsevich model, and let $\mathcal{Q}_k^{(g)}$ denote the number of bipartite rooted quadrangulations with $k$ faces on a genus-$g$ surface. Define the spectral data by

$$
x(z)=z-\frac{\lambda}{N}\frac{\varrho}{z+\varepsilon},\qquad y(z)=-x(-z),\qquad B(z_1,z_2)=\frac{dz_1dz_2}{(z_1-z_2)^2},
$$

$$
\varepsilon(e,\lambda)=\frac{1}{6}\left(4e+\sqrt{4e^2+12\lambda}\right),\qquad \varrho(e,\lambda)=\frac{N}{18\lambda}\left(2e\sqrt{4e^2+12\lambda}-4e^2+12\lambda\right).
$$

**Bipartite quadrangulation conjecture.** For $g>0$, the topological recursion for this spectral curve gives

$$
\frac{\omega^{TR}_{g,1}(\varepsilon)}{dR(\varepsilon)}=\frac{1}{R'(\varepsilon)}\operatorname{Res}_{q\to-\varepsilon\pm i\sqrt{\lambda\varrho}}\left(K_{\pm}(q,\sigma(q),\varepsilon)\,\omega_{g-1,2}(q,\sigma(q))\right)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\mathcal{Q}_k^{(g)}\frac{(-\lambda)^k}{(2e)^k},
$$

where $\sigma(q)=\varepsilon+\frac{\lambda}{N}\frac{\varrho}{q+\varepsilon}$ is the global Galois involution. The conjecture extends the observed genus-one and genus-two computations to arbitrary genus; the paper notes that it was checked for $g=2$ by computer algebra, while a general proof is not provided.
352588.gap: Need all-genus residue/count correspondence with full spectral and rooting normalizations. Genus1/2 do not imply arbitrary genus; actual definitions unread.

347732.title: Linear and quadratic loop equations for the quartic Kontsevich model
347732.literal:
Let $R:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ be the ramified covering defined by the model, let $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_{2d}$ be its ramification points, and let $\sigma_i$ be the corresponding local Galois involution near $\beta_i$. Define $\omega_{0,1}(z)=-R(-z)R'(z)\,dz$ and $\omega_{0,2}(u_1,z)=\frac{du_1\,dz}{(u_1-z)^2}+\frac{du_1\,dz}{(u_1+z)^2}$; for $2-2g-m<0$, define $\omega_{g,m}$ by the stated residue system. **Loop-equation conjecture.** For all $g\geq0$ and $m\geq1$, the meromorphic differentials $\omega_{g,m}$ are symmetric and satisfy, near every $\beta_i$, the linear loop equation

$$
\omega_{g,m}(u_1,\ldots,u_{m-1},z)+\omega_{g,m}(u_1,\ldots,u_{m-1},\sigma_i(z))=\mathcal{O}(z-\beta_i)\,dz
$$

and the quadratic loop equation

$$
\omega_{g-1,m+1}(u_1,\ldots,u_{m-1},z,\sigma_i(z))+\sum_{\substack{I_1\uplus I_2=\{u_1,\ldots,u_{m-1}\}\\g_1+g_2=g}}\omega_{g_1,|I_1|+1}(I_1,z)\omega_{g_2,|I_2|+1}(I_2,\sigma_i(z))=\mathcal{O}((z-\beta_i)^2)(dz)^2.
$$

The claim is motivated by the verified low-degree cases and would establish the loop-equation structure underlying blobbed topological recursion for the quartic model; the general assertion remains open in the supplied text.
347732.gap: Need full meromorphic symmetry plus BOTH local loop equations at every stable genus/arity. Definition of the source residue system and unstable terms unread.

336082.title: Lapid's conjecture on parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials
336082.literal:
Let $P_{u,w}$ be the Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials for symmetric groups, and let $H\simeq S_m\times\dots\times S_m$ be the parabolic subgroup of $S_{mn}$ of type $(m,\dots,m)$. For $w\in S_n$, let $\widetilde w\in S_{mn}$ be defined by $\widetilde w(mi-j)=mw(i)-j$ for $i=1,\dots,n$ and $j=0,\dots,m-1$. Write

$$
\sum_{u\in H}\operatorname{sgn} u\,P_{\widetilde xu,\widetilde w}=q^{{m\choose 2}(\ell(w)-\ell(x))}\widetilde P^{(m)}_{x,w}.
$$

For any $x,w\in S_n$ with $x\le w$, **Lapid's conjecture.** The polynomial $\widetilde P^{(m)}_{x,w}$ satisfies all of the following: it is a polynomial rather than a Laurent polynomial; $\widetilde P^{(m)}_{x,w}(0)=1$; $\widetilde P^{(m)}_{x,w}=\widetilde P^{(m)}_{xs,w}$ for every simple reflection $s$ of $S_n$ such that $ws<w$; and

$$
\deg\widetilde P^{(m)}_{x,w}=m\deg P_{x,w}.
$$

In particular, $\widetilde P^{(m)}_{x,w}=1$ if and only if $P_{x,w}=1$. The conjecture was motivated by representation-theoretic irreducibility results and computer calculations concerning parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials. It was verified numerically when $nm\le 12$ and proved in the paper for $m=2$ when $w$ is a Coxeter element of $S_n$ or of a parabolic subgroup; the general conjecture remains open in the supplied text.
336082.gap: Need simultaneous polynomiality, constant term, descent invariance and exact degree scaling for every x<=w and m. Generic KL positivity alone does not pay the alternating parabolic sum.

336580.title: Higher-order Macdonald positivity conjecture
336580.literal:
Let $\lambda^1,\dots,\lambda^r$ be partitions, and define the Macdonald cumulant by

$$
\kappa(\lambda^1,\dots,\lambda^r)(\bm{x};q,t):=\frac{\kappa(\tilde{H}_{\lambda^1}(\bm{x};q,t),\dots,\tilde{H}_{\lambda^r}(\bm{x};q,t))}{(q-1)^{r-1}}.
$$

Writing it in the Schur basis defines the multivariate $q,t$-Kostka numbers by

$$
\kappa(\lambda^1,\dots,\lambda^r):=\sum_{\mu}\tilde{K}^{(q,t)}_{\mu;\lambda^1,\dots,\lambda^r}\,s_\mu.
$$

**Higher-order Macdonald positivity conjecture.** For every partition $\mu$, the multivariate $q,t$-Kostka number $\tilde{K}^{(q,t)}_{\mu;\lambda^1,\dots,\lambda^r}$ is a polynomial in $q,t$ with nonnegative integer coefficients.

The conjecture strengthens the known polynomiality of Macdonald cumulants to Schur-positivity. The source says it was motivated by extensive computer simulations and remained unresolved there.
336580.gap: Need Schur coefficient nonnegativity of all normalized Macdonald cumulants. Polynomiality is explicitly weaker; no positivity mechanism derived.

328116.title: The Alexander polynomial coefficient inequality for rational cuspidal curves
328116.literal:
Let $C$ be a rational cuspidal curve of degree $d$ with critical points $z_1,\ldots,z_n$. Let $K_1,\ldots,K_n$ be the corresponding links of singular points, with Alexander polynomials $\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_n$, and let $G_1,\ldots,G_n$ be their gap sequences. Set

$$
g=|G_1|+|G_2|+\ldots+|G_n|
$$

so that $g$ is the genus of $K$. Write

$$
\Delta(t)=1+(t-1)g+(t-1)^2\sum_{j=0}^{2g-2}k_l
$$

and let $I=I_1\diamond I_2\diamond\ldots\diamond I_n$. **The Alexander polynomial coefficient inequality.** For every $j=0,\ldots,d-3$,

$$
k_{d(d-j-3)}\leq I\bigl(d(d-j-3)+1\bigr),
$$

with equality for $n=1$. This conjecture concerns restrictions on the Alexander polynomials and gap sequences of rational cuspidal curves; the equality case for one critical point was verified by Borodzik and Livingston, while the general case remains open in the supplied source.
328116.gap: Need the coefficient inequality for every rational cuspidal curve, with all source gap-convolution definitions. Printed polynomial expansion is malformed; no wording-based refutation proposed.

325290.title: Fernández de Bobadilla–Luengo–Melle-Hernández–Némethi conjecture on Alexander polynomials of rational cuspidal curves
325290.literal:
Let $C$ be a rational cuspidal curve of degree $d$ with critical points $z_1,dots,z_n$. Let $K_1,dots,K_n$ be the corresponding links of singular points, and let $Delta_1,dots,Delta_n$ be their Alexander polynomials. Set $Delta=Delta_1cdotdotscdotDelta_n$ and expand it as

$$
Delta(t)=1+\frac{(d-1)(d-2)}{2}(t-1)+(t-1)^2\sum_{j=0}^{2g-2}k_l t^l.
$$

**Fernández de Bobadilla–Luengo–Melle-Hernández–Némethi conjecture.** For every $j=0,dots,d-3$,

$$
k_{d(d-j-3)}\leq \frac{(j+1)(j+2)}{2},
$$

with equality when $n=1$. This conjecture gives constraints on the Alexander polynomials of the links of singular points of rational cuspidal curves. The source states that it was proposed in the cited work and verified for all known examples; the paper's theorem proves the one-singular-point case, while the general multiple-singularity statement is the relevant remaining conjectural form.
325290.gap: Need coefficient bound for arbitrary multiple singularities of an actual curve. Semigroup lists alone do not certify realizability; no source-own or later refutation authenticated.

324725.title: Koszul-duality conjecture for new identities of corresponding operations
324725.literal:
Let $\mathsf{Dias}$ and $\mathsf{Dend}=\mathsf{Dias}^!$ be the dual operads of associative dialgebras and dendriform algebras, respectively. For $n\leq 3$, multilinear identities of the Jordan diproduct in the free $\mathsf{Dias}$-algebra are consequences of right commutativity, $x(yz)-x(zy)\equiv 0$, and the pre-Jordan product in the free $\mathsf{Dend}$-algebra has no polynomial identities. Let $P_n$ be the $S_n$-module of multilinear right-commutative polynomials, with $Q_n\subseteq P_n$ the submodule of identities of the Jordan diproduct and $R_n\subseteq Q_n$ the submodule generated by identities in lower degrees. Let $P'_n$ be the $S_n$-module of multilinear nonassociative polynomials, with $Q'_n\subseteq P'_n$ the submodule of identities of the pre-Jordan product and $R'_n\subseteq Q'_n$ the submodule generated by identities in lower degrees. **Koszul-duality conjecture.** For every $n\geq 4$, there is an isomorphism of $S_n$-modules

$$
Q_n/R_n\cong Q'_n/R'_n.
$$

The conjecture explains the matching multiplicities of new identities for the Jordan diproduct and pre-Jordan product through the duality between associative dialgebras and dendriform algebras; the computed cases through degree $8$ support it, while the assertion in all degrees remains open.
324725.gap: Need all-degree S_n-module isomorphism of NEW-identity quotients, with lower-degree consequences removed. Koszul duality alone is not an argument for this quotient identification.

381078.title: Equality of Kirillov functions and irreducible characters for unitriangular groups
381078.literal:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $n\leq 12$, and let $\mathfrak{u}_n(q)^*$ be the dual of the Lie algebra of strictly upper-triangular $n\times n$ matrices over the finite field with $q$ elements. For $\lambda\in\mathfrak{u}_n(q)^*$, write $\psi_\lambda$ for the associated irreducible character, $\psi^{\mathrm{Exp}}_\lambda$ for the character obtained using the exponential construction, and $\xi_\lambda$ for the Kirillov function.

**The conjecture.** For every $\lambda\in\mathfrak{u}_n(q)^*$,

$$
\psi_\lambda=\psi^{\mathrm{Exp}}_\lambda=\xi_\lambda\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathrm{UT}_n(q)).
$$

This would show that, for $n\leq 12$, every irreducible character of the unitriangular group is obtained directly from a functional by the Kirillov construction. The statement is known for $q=2$ from computer calculations, but the source presents it as conjectural for general prime powers and suggests that a verification analogous to Evseev's computational work may be possible.
381078.gap: Need uniform all-prime-power character/Kirillov equality for every n<=12, with the actual source meanings of psi, exponential and Kirillov. No character tables/enumeration executed; source definitions unread.

380538.title: The forcing flexibility conjecture for automorphism-tower heights
380538.literal:
Let $V$ be the ground model. For a centreless group $G\in V$, let $\tau(G)$ be the least ordinal $\alpha$ such that the automorphism tower satisfies $G_\beta=G_\alpha$ for all $\beta>\alpha$, and let $\tau^{V^{\mathbb{P}}}(G)$ denote the value computed in the forcing extension $V^{\mathbb{P}}$. **Forcing flexibility conjecture.** Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be ordinals such that if $\alpha\geq 1$, then $\beta\geq 1$. Then there exist a centreless group $G$ and a notion of forcing $\mathbb{P}$ such that

$$
\tau(G)=\alpha\quad\text{and}\quad\tau^{V^{\mathbb{P}}}(G)=\beta.
$$

This conjecture asks whether the height of an automorphism tower can be changed to any prescribed ordinal height by passing to a suitable forcing extension, subject only to the fact that a nonzero height in the ground model remains nonzero in the extension. Earlier results showed that automorphism towers of centreless groups terminate and that their heights can increase or decrease in generic extensions, but the full simultaneous realization asserted here was not known from the supplied context.
380538.gap: Need simultaneous arbitrary ordinal forcing-height realization for centreless groups, not finite automorphism towers. Set-theoretic forcing and absoluteness bridge absent; no finite witness mechanism.

368433.title: Cohen–Macaulayness conjecture for the ASM embedding $A\mapsto 1\oplus A$
368433.literal: Let $A\in\operatorname{ASM}(n)$ be an alternating sign matrix, and let $1\oplus A\in\operatorname{ASM}(n+1)$ be the direct sum of the $1\times1$ identity matrix with $A$. **Cohen–Macaulayness conjecture.** The ASM $A$ is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if $1\oplus A$ is Cohen–Macaulay. The conjecture is motivated by the proved equidimensionality equivalence and by computer calculations over the rational numbers for $n\leq6$. The paper also proves that Cohen–Macaulayness of $1\oplus A$ implies Cohen–Macaulayness of $A$, leaving the converse as the substantive open direction.
368433.gap: Need depth preservation for A->1 direct sum A in actual ASM scheme/ideal. Equidimensionality and one direction do not pay the converse; no flatness or regular sequence established.

335530.title: Refined Hall–Littlewood filling identity conjecture
335530.literal:
Let $\mathrm{FIL}(\lambda,\tau,C)$ be the set of all fillings with shape $\lambda$, big basement $\tau$, and column sets $C$. Let $w_0$ be the decreasing basement permutation, and let $\tau\lambda$ and $\tau w_0$ denote the corresponding permuted shape and basement. Then

**Refined Hall–Littlewood filling identity conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{F\in\mathrm{FIL}(\lambda,w_0,C)}q^{\operatorname{maj}(F)}t^{\operatorname{inv}(F)}
=
\sum_{F\in\mathrm{FIL}(\tau\lambda,\tau w_0,C)}q^{\operatorname{maj}(F)}t^{\operatorname{inv}(F)}.
$$

This refinement is motivated by the known equality for modified Hall–Littlewood polynomials and by the authors' bijective proof of its $t=0$ case; the full equality is presented as a computer-supported conjecture.
335530.gap: Need a statistic-preserving bijection on every fixed column-set filling fiber at arbitrary q,t, beyond t=0. Actual filling/triple definitions unread.

381313.title: The shortest-identity conjecture for the transformation semigroup T_5
381313.literal:
Let $T_5$ be the full transformation semigroup on a set of five elements, and let

$$
(xy)^{3+\operatorname{lcm}(4)}(yx)^5(xy)^4 \equiv_5 (xy)^3(yx)^5(xy)^{4+\operatorname{lcm}(4)}.
$$

**Shortest-identity conjecture for $T_5$.** This identity is the shortest identity of $T_5$. The preceding theorem establishes that this identity holds, while the conjecture concerns its minimality; the paper notes that exhaustive search verifies the analogous minimality claim only for $k\leq 4$.
381313.gap: Need universal shortest-word LOWER bound in T5, not proof of the displayed identity which source already has. No exhaustive search/program allowed or performed; automaton distinguishability lemma unpaid.

353105.title: The generalized Kaprekar height conjecture
353105.literal:
Fix a base $b\geq 2$. Write every $u\geq 1$ uniquely as a tower of powers of $b$ ending in $0<\omega\leq 1$, and let $\operatorname{ht}(u)$ be the height of this tower. Let $K(n)$ denote the smallest number with exactly $n$ generators in base $b$. **Generalized Kaprekar height conjecture.**

(i) If $b=2$ and $n\geq 2$, then

$$
\operatorname{ht}(K(n))=\left\lceil\log_2(n)\right\rceil+3.
$$

(ii) If $b=3$ and $n\geq 3$, then

$$
\operatorname{ht}(K(n))=\left\lceil\log_2(n/5)\right\rceil+4.
$$

(iii) If $b\geq 4$ is even and $n\geq 2$, then

$$
\operatorname{ht}(K(n))=\left\lceil\log_2(n)\right\rceil+2.
$$

(iv) If $b\geq 5$ is odd and $n\geq 2$, then

$$
\operatorname{ht}(K(n))=\left\lceil\log_2(n)\right\rceil+1.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by computed tables and describes the rapid growth of $K(n)$ through exponential-tower height. The source offers computational evidence but no proof of these formulas.
353105.gap: Printed odd-base n=2 branch contradicts source own K(2)=b+1 and height3; zero-credit endpoint correction. Sustained corrected-range tower proof retained in KAPREKAR-ORDINARY-INVESTIGATION.md.

375678.title: The cubic plus-equation solution conjecture
375678.literal:
Let $a,b,x$ be positive integers with $a<b$, and consider

$$
(a^3+1)(b^3+1)=x^2.
$$

**Cubic plus-equation conjecture.** The only positive integer solutions are

$$
(a,b,x)\in\{(1,23,156),(6,26,1953),(20,362,616077)\}.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by a computer search with $n=3$ and $1\leq a<b\leq10^6$. The source does not state that the search establishes completeness beyond that range, and its general resolution status is not given.
375678.gap: Need an all-height integral-point completeness theorem for the cubic-plus Diophantine equation, or an exact additional solution personally proved. Factoring a^3+1 does not bound b or control all twists; no search/CAS run.

361986.title: The conjecture that β(N,l) depends only on l
361986.literal:
Let $N\geq 2$ and $1<l\mid N$. The homomorphism $\sigma_{N,l}$ has image $\operatorname{im}(\sigma_{N,l})=\beta(N,l)\mathbb{Z}$ for a unique positive integer $\beta(N,l)$. **Dependence conjecture.**

$$
\beta(N,l)=\beta(l,l).
$$

This would reduce the study of $\beta(N,l)$ to the diagonal values $\beta(l,l)$; the claim was verified for $l,N<1000$ by a SageMath program, but no proof or disproof is supplied here.
361986.gap: Need period attainment at every extra level; transfer only bounds beta(N,l)/beta(l,l) by the subgroup index. Explicit parabolics give only multiples of l-1. See SUSTAINED-ROUTES.md.

361987.title: The conjectural formula for β(N)
361987.literal:
Let $N\geq 2$ be an integer, and write $\beta(N)=\beta(N,N)$. **Formula conjecture.**

1. If $N\not\equiv 1,9\pmod{24}$, then $\beta(N)$ is periodic in $N$ with period $24$, with values given by the paper's table.
2. If $N\equiv 9\pmod{24}$, then $\beta(N)=8$ when $N$ is a perfect square and $\beta(N)=4$ otherwise.
3. If $N\equiv 1\pmod{24}$, then $\beta(N)=24$ when $N$ is a perfect square and $\beta(N)=12$ otherwise.

The first part was verified for $N\leq 960$, and the second and third parts for $N<3000$, by a SageMath program. The conjecture gives an explicit description of the image invariant $\beta(N)$, but remains unproved in the source.
361987.gap: Need exact diagonal integral-period gcd including primes>3 and valuations beyond24. Eta multipliers mod24 alone do not establish the image. Actual Newman prior proof unread. See SUSTAINED-ROUTES.md.

359519.title: Esser's coprimality conjecture for the large-index Calabi–Yau construction
359519.literal: For each integer $n\geq 2$, let $m'_n$ and $E_n$ be the explicitly defined integers associated with the weighted hypersurface construction. Two integers are **relatively prime** if their greatest common divisor is $1$. **Esser's coprimality conjecture.** The numbers $m'_n$ and $E_n$ are relatively prime. By the paper's criterion, this is equivalent to the associated quotient having index $m'_n$. The conjecture has been verified by computer in dimensions at most $30$; it remains open in general.
359519.gap: Odd-dimensional gcd reduces exactly to gcd((P+1)/2,v_2r), still unpaid; even dimensions need separate /3 and p=3 treatment. Descending w,g relations propagate nonzero terms. See SUSTAINED-ROUTES.md.
